summary: DEQ shall prioritize and expedite development of data center noise regulations consistent with existing statutory authority and applicable legislative direction, and shall establish a public process engaging affected communities, local governments, operators and public-health experts. Within 180 days DEQ shall provide a proposed accelerated timeline, workplan and stakeholder-engagement plan for the noise rulemaking.
text: DEQ shall prioritize and expedite the development of data center noise regulations consistent with DEQ's existing statutory authority and applicable legislative direction. DEQ shall establish a public process that meaningfully engages affected communities, local governments, data-center operators, public-health experts, and other stakeholders. Within 180 days of the date of this Executive Order, DEQ shall provide the Office of the Governor with a proposed accelerated timeline, workplan, and stakeholder-engagement plan for the noise-rulemaking process.

source.citation: Virginia Executive Order 22 (2026), Establishing New Nation-Leading Standards and Initiatives to Implement the Virginia Data Center Accountability Framework and Responding to Unprecedented Risk from Artificial Intelligence, signed September 18 2026

notes: Workplan due on or about March 17 2027. The order's recitals reference noise reduction measures already established by legislation, which is a pointer to existing Virginia statute not yet read into this corpus. If a state noise standard is adopted, Virginia joins the municipal acoustic provisions recorded for Phoenix, Chandler and Marana at a state level.
confidence_note: Sets no noise standard. Establishes no decibel limit, no measurement point, no measurement method, no measurement duration and no compliance obligation. The deliverable at 180 days is a plan for a rulemaking, not a rule. The existing legislative direction referenced in the recitals has not been identified or read.
